entries.title: Voyager 1 Interstellar Plasma Waves
entries.conversion_method: Plasma-wave electric-field oscillations measured by Voyager 1 were amplified into an audible soundtrack that preserves the measured amplitude and frequency content already within human hearing range.
entries.processing_notes: Not a musical sonification mapping of an image. JPL describes the waves as amplified instrument antenna signals.
entries.short_explanation: Instrument-derived plasma-wave signals from Voyager 1 in interstellar space, amplified into audible form.
entries.mapping_explanation: The soundtrack reproduces the amplitude and frequency of plasma waves detected by Voyager 1's plasma wave instrument. The waves can be amplified and played through a speaker because those frequencies already fall in the human hearing range.
entries.what_it_does_not_prove: This is not a microphone recording of sound traveling through vacuum, and it is not an exact target recording for most Solar System moons or planets.
entries.credits: NASA / JPL-Caltech. Voyager 1 Plasma Wave Subsystem data.
entries.attribution: NASA Jet Propulsion Laboratory Photojournal PIA17045
entries.accessibility_description: Spectrogram-style video of Voyager 1 plasma-wave detections with audible amplified plasma-wave signal.
entries.verification_notes: Source page: JPL PIA17045. Direct media HEAD/GET returns video/mp4 on assets.science.nasa.gov (final host assets.science.nasa.gov). Older photojournal.jpl.nasa.gov/archive/...mp4 now redirects to HTML and was rejected for playback.

entries.title: Vela Pulsar Sonification
entries.conversion_method: Radar-like clockwise image scan; brightness to volume; distance from center to pitch; Chandra X-ray and Hubble optical layers mapped to distinct synthesized timbres.
entries.processing_notes: Chandra bright inner region uses a low synth with ~11 Hz oscillations matching the pulsar period; outer X-ray/jet use wind-like sound; Hubble stars use plucked-synth notes.
entries.short_explanation: A data sonification of the Vela Pulsar region from Chandra and Hubble observations.
entries.mapping_explanation: Listen to a radar-like scan, clockwise from 12:00 of the image. Brightness is mapped to volume. Distance from the center is mapped to pitch (farther away is higher pitch). Chandra X-ray and Hubble optical data use different synthesized sounds.
entries.what_it_does_not_prove: This is not a microphone recording from space. Pitch and volume come from an intentional mapping of image brightness and position.
entries.credits: Chandra X-ray Center (CXC) with NASA's Universe of Learning; visualization scientist Dr. Kimberly Arcand (CXC); Dr. Matt Russo and Andrew Santaguida (SYSTEM Sounds).
entries.attribution: Chandra X-ray Center / Smithsonian Astrophysical Observatory / NASA
entries.accessibility_description: Sonification video scanning the Vela Pulsar multiwavelength image into sound.
entries.verification_notes: Official Chandra Universe of Sound page. Direct media returns video/mp4 on www.chandra.si.edu (final host www.chandra.si.edu).

entries.title: Crab Nebula Sonification
entries.conversion_method: Left-to-right image scan; each wavelength family maps to a different instrument family; vertical position to pitch; brightness to loudness.
entries.processing_notes: Chandra X-ray → brass; Hubble optical → strings; Spitzer infrared → woodwinds.
entries.short_explanation: A data sonification of the Crab Nebula combining Chandra, Hubble, and Spitzer data.
entries.mapping_explanation: The translation pans left to right. Each wavelength of light is paired with a different family of instruments. Light toward the top of the image is higher pitched; brighter light is louder.
entries.what_it_does_not_prove: This is a data sonification, not a microphone recording from the nebula.
entries.credits: Chandra X-ray Center (CXC) with NASA's Universe of Learning; Dr. Kimberly Arcand (CXC); Dr. Matt Russo and Andrew Santaguida (SYSTEM Sounds).
entries.attribution: Chandra X-ray Center / Smithsonian Astrophysical Observatory / NASA
entries.accessibility_description: Sonification video of the Crab Nebula multiwavelength composite.
entries.verification_notes: Official Chandra Universe of Sound page. Direct media returns video/mp4 on www.chandra.si.edu.

entries.title: Cassiopeia A Sonification
entries.conversion_method: Element distributions and high-energy structures are scanned outward from the center along multiple paths; intensity controls volume.
entries.processing_notes: Silicon, sulfur, calcium, and iron paths plus a jet path are mapped to distinct audio tracks.
entries.short_explanation: A data sonification of Cassiopeia A supernova remnant element maps from Chandra.
entries.mapping_explanation: Sounds are mapped to four elements in the debris as well as other high-energy data, moving outward from the center, with intensity controlling volume. A fifth path follows the upper-left jet.
entries.what_it_does_not_prove: This is not literal sound from the remnant; it is a sonification of X-ray data products.

entries.title: Galactic Center / Sagittarius A* Sonification
entries.conversion_method: Left-to-right scan of a Chandra/Hubble/Spitzer composite; vertical position to pitch; brightness to volume; compact sources as notes and extended clouds as evolving drone.
entries.processing_notes: Ensemble mix assigns different telescope layers to different sonic roles; crescendo near Sagittarius A*.
entries.short_explanation: A data sonification of the Milky Way's Galactic Center region, including Sagittarius A*.
entries.mapping_explanation: The translation begins on the left and moves right. Higher image positions are higher pitches; brighter light is louder. Stars and compact sources become individual notes; extended gas and dust produce an evolving drone.
entries.what_it_does_not_prove: This is not a recording of sound at the Galactic Center; it is a sonification of multiwavelength telescope data.
entries.credits: Chandra X-ray Center (CXC) with NASA's Universe of Learning; Dr. Kimberly Arcand (CXC); Dr. Matt Russo and Andrew Santaguida (SYSTEM Sounds).
entries.attribution: Chandra X-ray Center / Smithsonian Astrophysical Observatory / NASA
entries.accessibility_description: Sonification video of the Galactic Center multiwavelength composite including Sagittarius A*.
entries.verification_notes: Official Chandra Universe of Sound Galactic Center page. Direct media returns video/mp4 on www.chandra.si.edu.

entries.title: MSH 15-52 / PSR B1509-58 Sonification
entries.conversion_method: Bottom-to-top image scan of the pulsar-wind nebula. Chandra brightness maps to rough string-like sounds; the blast wave to firework-type pitches; IXPE X-ray polarization data to wind-like sounds; infrared survey data to synthesizer pitches. The pulsar light curve is heard as pulses almost 7 times per second, matching the measured pulse rate.
entries.short_explanation: A data sonification of the MSH 15-52 pulsar-wind nebula powered by PSR B1509-58, combining Chandra, IXPE, and infrared survey data.
entries.mapping_explanation: The scan goes from the bottom to the top. Chandra cloud brightness becomes rough string-like sounds; the blast wave uses firework-type pitches; IXPE data sound wind-like; infrared data map to synthesizer pitches. The collapsed core's brightness-over-time light curve is heard as pulses almost 7 times every second, as in the original timing data. This remains a data sonification, not a microphone recording.
entries.what_it_does_not_prove: This is not microphone audio from the nebula. Pitch, timbre, and pulsing come from intentional mappings of X-ray, infrared, and pulsar timing products.
entries.accessibility_description: Sonification video scanning MSH 15-52 from bottom to top with pulsed representation of PSR B1509-58.
entries.verification_notes: Official Chandra Universe of Sound page. Composite MP4 returns video/mp4 with ftyp on www.chandra.si.edu. Alternate tracks: sonify8_hand_chandra.mp4, sonify8_hand_ixpe.mp4, sonify8_hand_sources.mp4 deferred. Pulse rate documented as almost 7 Hz on the official page.

entries.title: M74 (Phantom Galaxy) Sonification
entries.conversion_method: Clockwise radar-like scan from about 12 o'clock. Distance from center controls pitch (farther from center is higher). Chandra, JWST, and Hubble layers use distinct timbres.
entries.short_explanation: A data sonification of face-on spiral galaxy M74 combining Chandra, JWST, and Hubble data.
entries.mapping_explanation: A clockwise radar-like scan starts around 12 o'clock. Distance from the center controls sound frequency, with light farther from the center heard at higher pitch. Chandra sources map to glassy ethereal and plucked sounds; Webb features use low/medium/high frequencies by structure size; Hubble optical data fill additional mapped layers in the composite.
entries.what_it_does_not_prove: This is not a recording of sound from M74. Pitch follows radial distance and brightness mappings chosen for the sonification.
entries.accessibility_description: Sonification video of M74 with clockwise radial pitch mapping.
entries.verification_notes: Official Chandra page. Composite MP4 verified video/mp4+ftyp. Alternates: sonify8_m74_hst.mp4, sonify8_m74_jwst.mp4, sonify8_m74_xray.mp4 deferred.

entries.title: Supernova 1987A Sonification
entries.conversion_method: Time-lapse of Chandra and Hubble observations (1999-2013) sonified while focus sweeps the image; brighter light maps to higher and louder notes; optical uses a higher pitch range than X-ray.
entries.short_explanation: A data sonification of SN 1987A's glowing gas ring evolving between 1999 and 2013 in Chandra and Hubble data.
entries.mapping_explanation: A time lapse of Chandra (blue) and Hubble (orange/red) observations from 1999 to 2013 shows a pre-explosion gas ring brightening as the shockwave passes. As focus sweeps the image, data become crystal singing-bowl tones with brighter light higher and louder. Optical notes use a higher range than X-rays so both can be heard together.
entries.what_it_does_not_prove: This is not live audio from the supernova. It sonifies multiyear telescope imagery of the remnant.
entries.accessibility_description: Sonification of SN 1987A multiwavelength time-lapse imagery.
entries.verification_notes: Official Chandra SN87A page. Composite sn87a_all.mp4 verified. Alternates sn87a_opt/xray deferred.

entries.title: M87 Sonification
entries.conversion_method: Radar-like clockwise scan from the 3 o'clock position. Distance from center maps to pitch; brightness to loudness; radio lower than X-ray; point sources as short plucked sounds.
entries.short_explanation: A data sonification of M87's black-hole jet environment using Chandra X-ray and VLA radio data.
entries.mapping_explanation: The image is scanned from the 3 o'clock position clockwise like a radar. Light farther from the center is higher pitched; brighter light is louder. Radio data are lower pitched than X-rays, reflecting their electromagnetic frequency ranges. Point-like X-ray sources play as short plucked sounds. This maps the jet and hot gas environment; it does not acoustically record the black hole itself.
entries.what_it_does_not_prove: The black hole was not recorded with a microphone. Sounds come from spatial and brightness mappings of X-ray and radio telescope products.
entries.accessibility_description: Sonification of M87 Chandra X-ray and VLA radio composite.
entries.verification_notes: Official Chandra M87 page. m87_all.mp4 verified. Alternates m87_xray/radio deferred. Separate M87 Jet page deferred.

entries.title: Andromeda Galaxy (M31) Sonification
entries.conversion_method: Left-to-right scan across stacked wavelength layers (X-ray through radio). Brightness controls volume; vertical position controls pitch; each band uses a different note range.
entries.short_explanation: A data sonification of the Andromeda Galaxy (M31) combining X-ray through radio telescope layers.
entries.mapping_explanation: Wavelength layers are stacked horizontally from X-rays at the top through ultraviolet, optical, infrared, and radio at the bottom. A left-to-right scan maps each band to a different note range from lower-energy radio up to high-energy X-rays. Source brightness controls volume and vertical location controls pitch.
entries.what_it_does_not_prove: This is not sound recorded in Andromeda. It sonifies multiwavelength image products of M31.
entries.accessibility_description: Sonification of Andromeda Galaxy multiwavelength composite.
entries.verification_notes: Official Chandra Andromeda page. Composite m31.mp4 verified. Bare alias 'andromeda' omitted to avoid constellation false matches.

entries.title: Jupiter Sonification
entries.conversion_method: Left-to-right scan. Chandra X-rays (including auroral regions and enhanced diffuse ring emission) map to woodwind-like sounds; Hubble infrared planet data add fuller instrumental textures; pitch descends across the bright equatorial band and Great Red Spot.
entries.short_explanation: A data sonification of Jupiter combining Chandra X-ray and Hubble infrared imagery — not literal planetary microphone audio.
entries.mapping_explanation: As the scan moves left to right, Chandra X-rays flanking the planet play as woodwind sounds. Over the planet, Hubble infrared data make the texture fuller. Because Jupiter is tilted, pitch descends across the bright equatorial band and Great Red Spot. Additional Chandra X-ray emission at the end sounds gusty/wind-like. These are mapped telescope data, not sounds recorded in Jupiter's atmosphere.
entries.what_it_does_not_prove: This is not a microphone recording from Jupiter. It sonifies Chandra and Hubble image products.
entries.accessibility_description: Sonification of Jupiter Chandra X-ray and Hubble infrared composite.
entries.verification_notes: Official Chandra Jupiter sound page + photo/2026/sonify11 collection. Composite verified.

entries.title: Saturn Sonification
entries.conversion_method: Right-to-left scan. Cassini optical rings map to a siren-like frequency following the ring arc; the planet body maps to lower dark synthetic bass; Chandra X-rays map to higher synthetic tones across planet, rings, and poles.
entries.short_explanation: A data sonification of Saturn combining Chandra X-rays with Cassini optical imagery of the planet and rings.
entries.mapping_explanation: The scan begins on the right and moves left. Saturn's rings (Cassini optical) produce a siren effect whose frequency follows the ring arc. The planet itself becomes lower dark synthetic bass tones, distinguishing rings from the globe. Chandra X-rays are higher synthetic tones marking high-energy activity across the planet, rings, and poles. This is telescope-data sonification, not literal Saturn microphone audio.
entries.what_it_does_not_prove: This is not a recording of sound on Saturn. It sonifies Chandra and Cassini image products.
entries.accessibility_description: Sonification of Saturn rings and planet with Chandra X-ray overlays.
entries.verification_notes: Media on www.chandra.si.edu verified video/mp4+ftyp. Mapping/credits from Chandra photo album sonify11 and NASA Planetary Parade article because sound/saturn.html body text incorrectly describes Uranus.

entries.title: Uranus Sonification
entries.conversion_method: Left-to-right scan. A cello traces the ring arc; optical reflected light from Keck maps note changes; Chandra reflected solar X-rays map to higher frequencies over the planet.
entries.short_explanation: A data sonification of Uranus combining Chandra X-ray and Keck optical data — not literal ice-giant microphone audio.
entries.mapping_explanation: Left to right, a cello traces Uranus's arcing ring. Notes then change with reflected optical light and position from Keck. Chandra X-rays (solar X-rays reflected from Uranus) are heard as higher frequencies over the pinkish planetary region. Apparent X-ray asymmetry may be an imaging/smoothing artifact per the official caption.
entries.what_it_does_not_prove: This is not a microphone recording from Uranus. It sonifies Chandra and Keck image products.
entries.accessibility_description: Sonification of Uranus Chandra X-ray and Keck optical composite.
entries.verification_notes: Official Chandra Uranus sound page. Composite verified video/mp4+ftyp.

entries.title: Southern Ring Nebula Sonification
entries.conversion_method: JWST NIRCam then MIRI views with light-frequency-to-sound-frequency color mapping; central stars marked by distinct notes near 15s and 44s.
entries.short_explanation: A JWST data sonification contrasting near-infrared and mid-infrared views of the Southern Ring Nebula.
entries.mapping_explanation: Colors map to sound pitches by converting light frequencies toward sound frequencies. Near-infrared uses a higher pitch range first; mid-infrared notes are lower overall for longer wavelengths. Distinct notes near 15 and 44 seconds mark the image centers: NIRCam emphasizes one clear central star clang; MIRI presents a low then higher note for the two central stars. Official page states this does not represent sounds recorded in space.
entries.what_it_does_not_prove: This is not sound recorded at the nebula. Two musicians mapped JWST image data to composed sound.
entries.accessibility_description: Sonification contrasting JWST NIRCam and MIRI Southern Ring Nebula images.
entries.verification_notes: Official Chandra/Webb Universe of Sound page. Composite nircam_miri verified.

entries.title: Stephan's Quintet Sonification
entries.conversion_method: Scan across Chandra+JWST data: background galaxies/stars as glass marimba; diffraction-spiked stars as crash cymbals; quintet galaxies as smoothly changing frequencies; Chandra shock X-rays as synthetic strings.
entries.short_explanation: A data sonification of Stephan's Quintet combining Chandra X-ray shock emission with JWST infrared galaxy structure.
entries.mapping_explanation: Pitch changes with brightness in different ways across layers. Webb background galaxies and foreground stars map to synthetic glass marimba notes; stars with diffraction spikes play as crash cymbals. The quintet galaxies themselves are smoothly changing frequencies as the scan passes. Chandra X-rays of a multi-million-degree shock wave are synthetic string sounds.
entries.what_it_does_not_prove: This is not microphone audio from the galaxy group. It sonifies Chandra and JWST image products.
entries.accessibility_description: Sonification of Stephan's Quintet Chandra and JWST composite.
entries.verification_notes: Official Chandra Stephan's Quintet page. stephansquintet_all.mp4 verified.
